The mechanical and claims lenses, every refuter and the synthesis failed on the session token limit, so the r1 findings below are raw reviewer output that was triaged by the author, not machine-verified.

findings.location: continuous_thermal_closure: true; result_5mm.unassigned_heat_W; notes[1]; design/README_CF1.md section 1 ('360 W 稳态验收点闭合于模型层面'); tools/thermal_cf1.py L110-115 module_heat
findings.claim: 360 W steady state closes: CHB 94.17 <= 105, carrier 80.12 <= 95, Tj 120.83 <= 150, with 'unassigned' heat merely listed.
findings.defect: 36 % of the increment's own accounted heat (33.26 W of 91.16+33.26 W: other_wiring_contacts 5.35, shared_contact 5.86, aux 0.05, THN 4.2, STOP 16.8, brake 1.0) is dropped from a model whose only radiators are the three modelled faces. Placing just the spec-listed 22 W (STOP+THN+brake) anywhere on those faces drives the CHB above its limit in the same solver, so the closure flag is contradicted by the model it cites. DESIGN_SPEC section 1 required closure OR a quantified gap; neither is given, whereas the parent screen (SPATIAL_RADIATOR_NETWORK_SCREEN.json unassigned_extra_heat_sensitivity) at least published a +5/+10 W sensitivity.
findings.evidence: Re-solve with thermal_cf1.solve_with_node at the acceptance point, extra heat spread over the three faces in proportion to area: +5 W -> CHB 97.23 / carrier 83.43; +10 W -> 100.38 / 86.66; +22 W -> CHB 107.59 (>105) / carrier 94.08 / Tj 134.79; +33.3 W -> CHB 113.99 / carrier 100.67 (>95) / Tj 141.37. Slope ~0.6 K/W. other_wiring_contacts (5.35 W = I_m^2 x 0.010 ohm, thermal_cf1.py L77/L92) is main-path loss that the module connectors/harness must dissipate, yet it is excluded from the node.

findings.claim: Strap R 0.9920 / 1.1665 K/W with carrier margin 14.88 K; exclusions listed as spreading in carrier and lugs, fasteners, pressure non-uniformity, radiation, expansion.
findings.defect: The link model omits terms the parent's own nominal link included and that are not in the exclusion list: through-conduction of the 8 mm lug and of the web between its inner face and its radiating outer sheet (parent SPATIAL screen link_nominal_1D_terms_K_W has wall_through = 0.0942 K/W; CF1 has nothing), and the 4 mm carrier plate spreading between the Q201 arch at S y 36 and the -Y contact centroid at S y -36. Together they consume more than half the stated carrier margin. verify_thermal_cf1.py 'strap_R_recomputed' (L35-40) is a verbatim copy of the same formula, so it cannot detect an omitted term.
findings.evidence: Even taking the declared faces at face value: -Y lug 8 mm@167 + web 29.65 mm@130 over 1000 mm2 = 0.276 K/W; +Y 8 mm + 16.65 mm over 1080 mm2 = 0.163 K/W. Re-solve with these added: carrier 83.17 C, Tj 123.87. Adding a 1-D full-width plate spreading term 0.072/(167*0.004*0.132)=0.817 K/W on the -Y path: carrier 88.22 C, Tj 128.93 (margin 6.8 K instead of 14.9 K). Parent link terms for comparison: bottom_foot_through 0.076, riser 0.342, horizontal_arm 0.311, TIM 0.133, wall_through 0.094.
findings.suggested_fix: Add lug and web through-conduction terms to _link_R (read web thickness from the solid, not the bbox), add a carrier-plate spreading estimate or a second carrier node, list any remaining omissions explicitly, and make verify recompute R from the STEP-derived dimensions rather than re-evaluating the identical expression.
findings.disposition_note: lug-through, web-through (skin / stiffener gap / half plate from the probe) and a 1-D carrier-spreading term added; terms itemised in strap_R_terms_K_W; verify recomputes from the geometry file with its own arithmetic (term list shared, disclosed)

findings.location: L255 energy_balance_all_cases counterexample; L164-167 convergence test; verify_thermal_cf1.py L53-60 energy_balance_all_cases_le_1e-6W
findings.claim: Counterexample 'energy_balance_all_cases' detected (max 4.13e-9 W < 1e-6) and verify 'recomputes' the energy balance per case.
findings.defect: Neither is a test that can fail. The Newton loop only exits when |radiated-heat| < 5e-9 W (L165), so every converged case satisfies a criterion 200x looser than its own stop condition; the observed maximum 4.13e-9 W is simply the last iterate below 5e-9. The verify check subtracts two numbers the solver wrote (net_outward_W, input_W) and re-solves nothing, so it also cannot fail independently. The plan asked for a rejection test ('能量残差 >1e-6 时拒绝'); no unbalanced case is injected and no rejection path exists (if 80 iterations are exhausted only residual_max < 1e-8 is asserted, L168, not balance).
findings.evidence: COUNTEREXAMPLES.json energy_balance_all_cases.max_abs_W = 4.126e-9 (same order as the 5e-9 loop threshold); VALIDATION.json check 11 worst_abs_W identical value; README section 4 describes verify as '复算能量平衡（每工况 < 1e-6 W）'.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn the energy check into an independent recomputation (rebuild area*(eps*sigma*T^4-incoming) from a stored temperature field, or re-solve one case) and add a genuine negative control (e.g. a case with the node heat deliberately omitted from the RHS must be flagged); drop it from the 'counterexamples' list otherwise.
findings.disposition_note: ACCEPTANCE_FIELD_CF1.json stores T/area/incoming/heat; verify recomputes radiated-vs-input from the field (independent of solver totals) and shows a +1 K perturbation is detected; node link heats recomputed from the field vectors

findings.location: strap_degraded_20KW_carrier_exceeds; released_state_folded_wings_raises_CHB (thermal_cf1.py L251-254)
findings.claim: Two falsification tests detect a degraded strap and the released-state penalty.
findings.defect: Both are demonstrations of built-in behaviour rather than tests that probe a failure mode. With two 20 K/W straps in parallel the node temperature is the linear identity T_patch + Q*R/2 (27.46 W x 10 K/W = 274.6 K above the ~65 C patches = 339.9 C), so 'detected' is guaranteed for any R above ~4.5 K/W; the plan's stated control (R -> 1e6, i.e. link absent) was replaced by R = 20. The released-state control passes because the released grid blocks ~90 % of both Y faces versus 26-31 % (RADIATOR_MESH_VIEW_SCREEN mean blocked_fraction 0.899/0.903 vs 0.257/0.309); it only proves the state key is read.
findings.evidence: COUNTEREXAMPLES.json carrier_C 339.92 with threshold CARRIER_LIMIT+50 = 145; released_CHB 115.72 vs service 94.00, threshold +10 K.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep them as sanity checks but label them as such; add real negative controls (e.g. wrong patch face id must move the lug heat to a different sheet and be detected by the per-sheet net_outward split; a patch centre outside the face must raise the Sheet.weights assertion).
findings.disposition_note: the two built-in behaviours relabelled sanity_checks; three real negative controls added (wrong patch face moves 5.4 W between the Y faces; off-face patch refused; zero strap R refused)

findings.location: L138-139 (L rebuilt from L.data with L.nonzero() indices), L145-154 (link/node link assembly without the parent's finite-positive-R assert)
findings.claim: solve_with_node = parent solve plus one non-radiating node.
findings.defect: The lumped-node insertion itself is correct (v = +1 at node, -weights on patch; outer(v,v)/R symmetric; node area 0 so no radiation; node_link heat sign node-to-patch positive; residual row for the node = sum (T_n - Tbar_patch)/R - Q). Two robustness points: rebuilding L pairs L.data with L.nonzero() indices, which raises a shape error if any stored entry is an explicit zero (works today only because no g is zero); and the parent's assert that link R is finite and positive was dropped, so a zero or negative strap R would produce a singular/indefinite system rather than a clear failure.
findings.evidence: Verified against spatial_radiator_network.solve; acceptance iterations=5, residual 4.9e-13 W.
findings.suggested_fix: Use L.tocoo() for the resize and restore the R assert for links and node_links.
findings.disposition_note: block_diag rebuilt via COO row/col; finite-positive R asserted for links and node links

findings.location: lines 58-59 (filter `r['y0'] < 10.0`), results/pcb/CURRENT_DENSITY_CF1.json cf1.worst_forward_current_density_A_mm2, README_CF1.md §3 table row '正向最坏电流密度 29.1 A/mm²'
findings.claim: Worst forward current density is 29.1 A/mm² ≤ 35 A/mm² (VALIDATION check copper_loss_and_density_acceptance, DELIVERY_STATUS_CF1.json pcb.worst_forward_density_A_mm2).
findings.defect: The 29.1 figure is computed only on the five 8 mm bands. The two Q201 pad-entry stubs that the build adds (build_pcb_cf1.py:93 PAD_STUB_Q201_DRAIN x57.6-61.3 y15-17, 3.7 mm wide; :95 PAD_STUB_Q201_SOURCE x62.8-67.0 y15-17, 4.2 mm wide) are excluded by the y0<10 filter with the comment 'pad-entry stubs ... are not series conductors'. They are series conductors: the MAIN_SENSE band ends at y=15 and Q201 pad 2 copper starts at y=15.5 (pad bbox 57.6-61.3 x 15.5-18.5), so the whole 24.44 A crosses the 3.7 mm x 0.105 mm stub section; the project's own negative control (b) proves it (removing the stub -> DRC 'Missing connection between PTH pad 2 [WP10_MAIN_SENSE] of Q201 and Polygon'). J_drain = 24.44/(3.7*0.105) = 62.9 A/mm²; J_source = 24.44/(4.2*0.105) = 55.4 A/mm² - both above the 35 A/mm² limit. The V29 parent model counted the equivalent 2.6 mm necks to the same pad centres as MAIN_FORWARD_NECK (134 A/mm²), and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN Task 2 explicitly lists the '补 (59.45,11)→(59.45,17) 3.7' and '(64.9,12)→(64.9,17) 4.2' stubs as forward-path segments, so excluding them is a silent redefinition of the criterion.
findings.evidence: current_density_cf1.py:59 `if r['net'] in FORWARD and r['layer']=='F.Cu' and r['y0'] < 10.0 ...`; build_pcb_cf1.py:92-95 band (46.2,7.0,61.3,15.0) + stub (57.6,15.0,61.3,17.0); pcbnew read-back Q201 pad 2 size 3.7x3.0 drill 2.7x2.0 bbox y 15.5-18.5; negative_cf1_no_drain_stub_DRC.json unconnected_items[0]; V29 segments 'WP10_MAIN_SENSE (59.45,10)->(59.45,17) 2.6 MAIN_FORWARD_NECK'; arithmetic 24.44/(3.7*0.105)=62.9.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the two stubs (and any other neck between band and pad) as MAIN_FORWARD_NECK segments with length = band edge to pad edge (0.5 mm) or to pad centre (2 mm, parent convention) and report the true worst density; either widen the entry (e.g. taper the band into a full-pad-width fan-out plus B.Cu PTH-side copper on both Q201 power pads) or re-state the criterion explicitly as 'bands only' in DESIGN_SPEC/README with the neck densities disclosed alongside.
findings.disposition_note: necks modelled as MAIN_FORWARD_NECK; worst neck 62.9 A/mm2 reported; VALIDATION check forward_current_density_le_35_including_Q201_pad_entry_necks now FAILS by design; band-only 29.1 A/mm2 reported separately; open item in DELIVERY_STATUS

findings.location: docstring lines 3-7, cf1_segments() lines 55-69 vs parent_segments() lines 36-43; results/pcb/CURRENT_DENSITY_CF1.json acceptance.loss_reduction_vs_V29_recorded = 0.5744
findings.claim: Main-path copper loss reduced 57.4 % vs V29 (R20 8.578 -> 3.651 mΩ), 'apples-to-apples' series model.
findings.defect: The parent side is the V29 15-segment centreline model including two 2.6 mm necks (0.663 + 0.388 mΩ); the CF1 side drops the corresponding necks entirely (see CF1-PCB-01) and treats each band as a conductor of its full x-extent. The two sides therefore use different path definitions. Recomputed R20 from CURRENT_DENSITY_CF1.json segments: forward 0.2853+0.1991+0.1765+0.3099+0.5346 = 1.5054 mΩ, return 2*0.2258+2*0.3694+0.9553 = 2.1457 mΩ, total 3.6510 mΩ (matches). Adding the omitted necks at the parent convention (to pad centre, 2 mm): r20(2,3.7,0.105)=0.0887 mΩ + r20(2,4.2,0.105)=0.0782 mΩ -> 3.818 mΩ, loss20 = 400*3.818e-3*1.3144 = 2.008 W, reduction 55.5 %; at band-edge-to-pad-edge (0.5 mm) -> 3.693 mΩ, 56.9 %. The ≥40 % criterion survives, but the stated 57.4 % and the 'not series conductors' justification are not model-consistent. (Band x-extent lengths over-count length vs the actual entry/exit points by roughly 0.25 mΩ in CF1's disfavour, so the net bias is small but undocumented.) thermal_cf1.py line 54 consumes the 3.651 mΩ figure as COPPER_CF1_20C.
findings.evidence: V29 R20_ohm 0.008578 with MAIN_FORWARD_NECK entries; CF1 segments list has no neck entries; docstring 'Vias are ignored (conservative: no credit)' and code comment line 58.
findings.suggested_fix: Model the CF1 forward path with the same segment definition as V29 (band + neck to pad centre), report both R20 numbers, and restate the reduction; propagate the corrected R20 into thermal_cf1.py (effect on carrier temperature is < 0.2 K, but the receipt chain must be consistent).
findings.disposition_note: necks booked to the pad centre (V29 convention): R20 3.818 mOhm, reduction 55.5 % (bands-only 57.4 % also shown); thermal_cf1.py consumes the corrected R20
